source_location: Results: Characterizing Aβ42-Induced Hyperexcitability; Figure 1C–D caption
extraction: Numeric text explicitly reported in article; no figure digitization or individual observations reconstructed
preparation: Primary neurons dissociated from late-gastrula embryos, aged nine days in culture; article describes likely larval-stage neurons

protocol.outcome: injected current at first action potential
protocol.experimental_unit: recorded neuron; independence of culture batches not specified in this extraction

uncertainty_note: The extracted Figure 1 text reports +/- without an explicit error-type definition at that location; retain reported_plusminus rather than invent a CI or raw samples. Other figure captions label SEM, but do not assume this proves Figure 1's convention.
proposed_use: Calibrate a preparation-specific single-cell current-ramp response, not the full adult MaleCNS disease parameters
independent_targets: Dependence of first-spike latency on initial membrane potential in a pulse protocol (Figure 1E–F); new protocol, although same paper and not assured independent samples
Kv4 restoration effects on potassium currents (Figure 4); requires a conductance model and independent quantitative data extraction
mapping_limitations: 35.9-to-19.5 pA ratio cannot be applied directly to a voltage threshold; capacitance, leak, holding potential and channel kinetics matter
Changing a LIF threshold can match one summary without identifying Kv4 causality
Kaldun 2021 uses Arctic Aβ42 and adult memory assays; it is a different transgene/preparation, not paired measurements from these cells
Kv4 loss alone did not reproduce observed neurodegeneration, so do not equate an excitability proxy with neuron death
